thread:
maya: quick heads-up — seeing a spike of Xid 13 on a10s in ap-south1 starting ~02:40 UTC. pattern: batchsize=1, short token requests from low-priority tenants. looks correlated with cost-fallthrough routing to cheaper hosts. anyone else noticing this?
jon: saw infra-bot alerts too. logs look like nv decode aborts, not ECC. snippet:```[2026-03-19T02:40:12Z] host-az3-045 gpu0 Xid 13 decode abort seq=1245 tenant=tenant-42 batch=1 token_len=18```
kevin: that smells like micro-bursting + small-batch thrash. cheap routing tends to pack lots of tiny requests on same card -> context-switch pressure. can cause driver-level decode aborts. recommend checking batch-shape histogram.
lena: query I ran: `SELECT host, COUNT(*) FROM gpu_errors WHERE xid=13 AND region='ap-south1' GROUP BY host ORDER BY COUNT DESC LIMIT 10` -> 6 hosts hit, top is host-az3-045 (32 events in last 30m).
ops-bot: automated: host-az3-045 soft-drain scheduled by policy after 3 Xid13s in 15m. action=cordon + migrate low-priority.
jon: can we tweak routing to avoid packing small-batches on one card? e.g. spread low-priority batchsize<=1 across all available GPUs rather than filling cheapest first. Also consider temporary fallback to CPU/h100 for those tenants.
kevin: fallback to h100 will increase infra costs ~3-5x per token. but benefits: reduces error churn and avoids potential replacement/capacity loss. need cost vs replacement/proactive-repair calc.
lena: rough numbers: 50k small requests/day * avg 25 tokens => routing to h100 adds approx $1500/mo based on current price model. replacing a flaky A10 ~ $3k+ labor + lost capacity while OOO. might be cheaper to absorb short-term h100 routing.
maya: proposed plan: 1) soft-drain top 6 hosts and monitor 2) add routing rule to spread batchsize=1 low-priority across N hosts (N=10) 3) create Xid13 cohort alert correlated with tag `batchshape:single` and `route:cost-fallback` so we get early warning. Kevin, can you draft the routing PR + alert?
kevin: I'll draft PR and alert. will include a knob to opt-out per-tenant for latency-sensitive ones. also will add a simple Kusto query to the runbook: `gpu_errors | where xid==13 and batchsize==1 | summarize count() by host, bin(timestamp, 5m)` and a follow-up step to soft-drain after 3 sig events.
infra-bot: noted. maintenance window tentatively scheduled Thu 03:00 UTC for host-az3-045 if metrics don't improve.
maya: thanks all :thumbsup: i'll update the oncall and post the short checklist in #incidents if we escalate.
